comments.author: martinfleis
comments.body:
Thanks for the report. It is bit of a corner case as np.nan is technically a float not a geometry object or None. But given this works, the snippet above should likely too.

```py
gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    data=[[np.nan]],
    columns=["something"],
    geometry=[np.nan],
    crs="EPSG:4326",
)
```

Fix is coming up.

comments.author: zmoon
comments.body:
Thanks for the swift response @martinfleis , I agree it is an unusual case, I wouldn't think it would come up often. I only noticed because I was creating some data in a test that way.

Looking at the PR and experimenting a bit more, I would note that in v1.0.1 it also works for longer columns where `np.nan` is the only unique value, not just size-one.
```python
gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    data=np.full((10, 2), np.nan),
    columns=["geometry", "something"],
    crs="EPSG:4326",
)
```

Same with a mix of null types:
```python
gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    {
        "geometry": [np.nan, None, pd.NA],
        "something": [np.nan, np.nan, np.nan],
    },
    crs="EPSG:4326",
)
```

comments.author: martinfleis
comments.body: Thanks. I have updated the PR. I am still not sure if this is a behaviour we should encourage but given our geometry sanitisation deals with it in other cases, no need to disallow it here.
